facts.title: Experience League: Getting Started with the Migration Journey to AEM as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: Begin by determining if your deployment is ready to be moved to AEM as a Cloud Service with the Readiness Phase
facts.supports: The first phase of Adobe's documented migration journey is the Readiness Phase, which checks whether an existing AEM deployment is ready to move.

facts.title: Experience League: Getting Started with the Migration Journey to AEM as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: Next, make your code and content cloud ready with the Implementation Phase
facts.supports: The second phase is the Implementation Phase, where code and content are made cloud ready.

facts.title: Experience League: Getting Started with the Migration Journey to AEM as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: After everything is in place, you can perform the migration with the Go-Live Phase
facts.supports: The third phase is the Go-Live Phase, where the migration is performed (a Post Go-live Phase follows).

facts.title: Experience League: Overview to Cloud Acceleration Manager
facts.quote: Cloud Acceleration Manager is a cloud-based application designed to guide your IT teams throughout the transition journey starting from planning to going live on Cloud Service.
facts.supports: Cloud Acceleration Manager is Adobe's application that guides the move to AEM as a Cloud Service from planning to go-live.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview to Best Practices Analyzer
facts.quote: This tool generates a report that identifies areas of potential refactoring, which is the first step in the transition journey to AEM as a Cloud Service.
facts.supports: The Best Practices Analyzer runs against an existing AEM deployment and reports what must be refactored before moving to AEM as a Cloud Service.

facts.title: Experience League: Implementation Phase
facts.quote: Before you start, you must familiarize yourself with Cloud Manager since it is the sole mechanism for deploying code to AEM as a Cloud Service.
facts.supports: Cloud Manager is the only way to deploy code to AEM as a Cloud Service.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview to Content Transfer Tool
facts.quote: The Content Transfer Tool is a tool developed by Adobe that can be used to initiate the migration of existing content from a source AEM instance (on-premise or AMS) to the target AEM Cloud Service instance.
facts.supports: The Content Transfer Tool moves content from an existing AEM instance (on-premise or Adobe Managed Services) to an AEM as a Cloud Service instance; its source is AEM.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview to Content Transfer Tool
facts.quote: The Content Transfer Tool has a feature that supports differential content top-up where it is possible to transfer only changes made since the previous content transfer activity.
facts.supports: The Content Transfer Tool supports differential (top-up) transfers of only the changes since the last transfer.

facts.title: Experience League: Prerequisites for Content Transfer Tool
facts.quote: Content Transfer Tool can be run on AEM 6.3 or higher versions only.
facts.supports: The Content Transfer Tool runs on a source AEM instance at version 6.3 or higher, so it does not apply to a non-AEM CMS.

facts.title: Experience League: AEM as a Cloud Service content migration FAQ
facts.quote: Out of the box Bulk Import Service for Assets (S3/Azure → AEMaaCS)
facts.supports: Of the three content migration methods Adobe lists for AEM as a Cloud Service (Content Transfer Tool and Package Manager, both from AEM, and Bulk Import), the only one not sourced from AEM is the Bulk Import Service, and it brings in assets from S3 or Azure storage, not pages.

facts.title: aem.live: Importing Content
facts.quote: You start from an existing web page (the DOM is the input).
facts.supports: The AEM Importer works from the rendered pages of an existing website, so it does not depend on which CMS the source site runs.

facts.title: aem.live: Importing Content
facts.quote: The importer creates a docx document, a content package, or HTML for you.
facts.supports: The AEM Importer outputs docx files (document-based authoring), a content package (AEM authoring with the Universal Editor) or HTML (Document Authoring), all for Edge Delivery Services projects.

facts.title: aem.live: Importing Content
facts.quote: Using AEM’s package manager or the AEM Import Helper tool to import the JCR package to start your site with AEM authoring and the Universal Editor.
facts.supports: Imported content can be loaded into AEM as a Cloud Service author as a JCR package, for sites authored in the Universal Editor and delivered by Edge Delivery Services.

facts.title: aem.live: Frequently Asked Questions
facts.quote: Yes, Edge Delivery Services supports content migration from various platforms, including WordPress, Unsplash, Contentful, other AEM instances, and more.
facts.supports: Adobe states Edge Delivery Services supports content migration from non-AEM platforms such as WordPress and Contentful.

facts.title: Experience League: Experience Modernization Agent Overview
facts.quote: Supports migrations from a wide range of CMS platforms, legacy AEM, or design systems (like Figma) into production-capable Edge Delivery Services projects
facts.supports: The Experience Modernization Agent migrates sites from other CMS platforms, and its target is Edge Delivery Services.

facts.title: Experience League: Experience Modernization Agent Overview
facts.quote: The agent does not support the following targets. AEM publish environments where sites use HTL-based delivery
facts.supports: The Experience Modernization Agent cannot migrate into a traditional AEM Sites publish (HTL) implementation. Note: this quote runs from a list heading into its first list item.

facts.title: Experience League: AOE Delivery of the Experience Modernization Agent
facts.quote: Any CMS platform such as WordPress, Drupal, Sitecore, legacy AEM, SharePoint, or custom solutions can serve as a source. Source content must be publicly accessible over the internet as static HTML.
facts.supports: In Adobe's engineer-led (AOE) delivery of the agent, any CMS can be the source as long as the content is publicly reachable static HTML; the page states all such migrations target Edge Delivery Services.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: Run an end-to-end production pipeline with functional and UI testing to ensure an always current AEM product experience.
facts.supports: Adobe's go-live checklist starts with a full production pipeline run including functional and UI testing.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: Ensure that the DNS cutover does not introduce unexpected problems. Create a test subdomain to connect your production instance to before you go-live and do a round of UAT testing.
facts.supports: Adobe recommends rehearsing the DNS cutover on a test subdomain with UAT before go-live.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: Perform tests in a stage environment. It has the same sizing as production.
facts.supports: Performance and security tests are run in the stage environment, which is sized like production.

facts.title: Experience League: Go-Live
facts.quote: Also, you need to plan for a content freeze when the final content top-up is scheduled.
facts.supports: A content freeze is planned for the final content top-up before go-live (this applies when content is migrated from AEM with the Content Transfer Tool).

facts.title: Experience League: Code Quality Testing
facts.quote: Code quality testing evaluates your application code based on a set of quality rules. It is the primary purpose of a code-quality only pipeline and is executed immediately following the build step in all production and non-production pipelines.
facts.supports: Cloud Manager runs a code quality gate after the build step in every pipeline.

facts.title: aem.live: Go-Live Checklist
facts.quote: In most migrations there are legacy URLs that are retired. Make sure those are reflected in your redirects spreadsheet
facts.supports: For Edge Delivery Services, the go-live checklist calls for redirects for retired legacy URLs.

facts.title: Experience League: Universal Editor Introduction
facts.quote: The Universal Editor is a versatile visual editor that is part of Adobe Experience Manager Sites. It enables authors to perform what-you-see-is-what-you-get (WYSIWYG) editing of any headless or headful experience.
facts.supports: The Universal Editor is part of AEM Sites and gives authors WYSIWYG editing.

facts.title: Experience League: Templates to Create Pages that are Editable with the Page Editor
facts.quote: When an author creates a page, they must select a template, which is used as the basis for the new page. The template defines the structure of the resultant page, any initial content, and the components that can be used when editing the page in the Page Editor.
facts.supports: Authors create pages from templates that set the page structure, initial content and allowed components.

facts.title: Experience League: Core Components Introduction
facts.quote: The Core Components are a set of standardized Web Content Management (WCM) components for AEM to speed up development time and reduce maintenance cost of your websites.
facts.supports: Core Components are Adobe's standard set of page components for AEM Sites.

facts.title: Experience League: Embed a Form on Your Website
facts.quote: Access a form’s embed code to host it on your own website.
facts.supports: A Marketo Engage form has embed code for hosting it on a company's own website.

facts.title: Experience League: Embed a Form on Your Website
facts.quote: The form must be approved for the embed code to be available.
facts.supports: Prerequisite: the Marketo form must be approved before its embed code is available.

facts.title: Experience League: Embed a Form on Your Website
facts.quote: Form Prefill does not work when using the form embed code on your own pages or a Marketo landing page.
facts.supports: Limit: Marketo form prefill does not work for a form embedded with the embed code.

facts.title: Experience League: JavaScript API (Marketo Developer Guide)
facts.quote: Forms 2.0 lets marketers create web forms without programming knowledge. Forms can reside on Marketo landing pages or be embedded on any page of your website.
facts.supports: Marketo Forms 2.0 forms can be embedded on any page of the company's website, not only on Marketo landing pages.

facts.title: Experience League: Lead Tracking (Marketo Developer Guide)
facts.quote: When one of these events occurs, Marketo associates the cookie and all related web activity with the known lead.
facts.supports: Filling out a Marketo form is one of the listed events that ties a visitor's tracked web activity to a known lead in Marketo (the other listed events are arriving from a tracked Marketo email link and a REST Associate Lead call).

facts.title: aem.live: Frequently Asked Questions
facts.quote: Yes, Marketo forms can be embedded in Edge Delivery Services pages using the Marketo Forms API or iframe embed codes
facts.supports: Adobe states Marketo forms can be embedded in Edge Delivery Services pages.

facts.title: Experience League: How to Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: Integrating AEM Forms with Adobe Marketo Engage enables users to leverage the capabilities of Marketo Engage to create business logic from captured data and automate workflows, including smart campaigns and email automation. The configured form can send captured data to Marketo Engage for processing.
facts.supports: An AEM Forms adaptive form can send captured data to Marketo Engage for smart campaigns and email automation.

facts.title: Experience League: How to Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: A valid Adobe Marketo Engage license
facts.supports: Prerequisite listed by Adobe for connecting Marketo Engage with AEM Forms: a valid Marketo Engage license.

facts.title: Experience League: How to Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: AEM only supports the People(Leads) database among the various Marketo databases.
facts.supports: Limit: the AEM Forms integration works with Marketo's People (Leads) database only.

facts.title: Experience League: How to configure submit action to Marketo Engage for forms?
facts.quote: Adaptive Forms editor provides the Submit to Marketo Engage submit action to send Adaptive Forms data to Adobe Marketo Engage for processing.
facts.supports: The Submit to Marketo Engage submit action sends adaptive form data to Marketo Engage.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to AEM Forms as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: The organization can use AEM Forms as a Cloud Service to create digital forms, connect forms to existing data sources, integrate forms with Adobe Sign to add e-signatures to forms, and generate Document of Record (DoR) to archive submitted forms as PDF files.
facts.supports: AEM Forms adds data source connections, e-signatures through Adobe Sign and a Document of Record PDF of the submitted form.

facts.title: Experience League: How to Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: Supports a built-in Rule Editor for adding logic and conditions.
facts.supports: AEM Forms has a built-in Rule Editor for form logic and conditions (from Adobe's table comparing AEM Forms with other form solutions).

facts.title: Experience League: How to Integrate Marketo Engage with AEM Forms?
facts.quote: Offers a Prefill service to auto-populate form data.
facts.supports: AEM Forms has a Prefill service that auto-populates form data (same comparison table).

facts.title: Experience League: AEM Adaptive Forms Core Components Introduction
facts.quote: They also include features like validation, conditional logic, and responsive design, which can be used to create forms that are user-friendly and easy to use.
facts.supports: Adaptive Forms Core Components include validation, conditional logic and responsive design.

facts.title: Experience League: Introduction to the Architecture of Adobe Experience Manager as a Cloud Service
facts.quote: AEM as a Cloud Service is made up of high-level solutions such as AEM Sites, AEM Assets, and AEM Forms. These services are licensed individually, but can be used in collaboration.
facts.supports: AEM Forms is licensed separately from AEM Sites within AEM as a Cloud Service.

facts.title: aem.live: Frequently Asked Questions
facts.quote: Yes, with a valid AEM Forms license, Edge Delivery Services supports AEM Forms through the Adaptive Forms Block
facts.supports: Using AEM Forms on Edge Delivery Services needs a valid AEM Forms license.

not_found: A1: Adobe's documented "migration journey" (Readiness, Implementation, Go-Live, Post Go-live) is written for moving an existing on-premise or Adobe Managed Services AEM installation to AEM as a Cloud Service. No equivalent phased journey for a customer coming from a non-AEM CMS was found under experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/migration-journey/.

A3: Nothing found on Experience League for moving page content from a non-AEM CMS (WordPress, Sitecore, Drupal, custom) into a traditional AEM Sites as a Cloud Service implementation (Core Components, HTL, publish tier). The content migration FAQ lists only Content Transfer Tool (AEM 6.3+), Package Manager (AEM) and Bulk Import Service for Assets (S3/Azure). The AEM Importer and the Experience Modernization Agent both target Edge Delivery Services (document authoring, Document Authoring, or AEM authoring with the Universal Editor).

A3: No Adobe page found with a connector or tool specific to Sitecore or Drupal; they are named only as possible sources on the AOE delivery page. No page-creation OpenAPI for AEM Sites was found (web search only; the Content Fragment OpenAPIs exist but were not quoted).

A4: No single AEM as a Cloud Service page quoted on redirects; the cloud go-live checklist only mentions checking "proper link redirection" during UAT. The redirects quote is from the Edge Delivery Services go-live checklist on aem.live.

B1: The Marketo "Embed a Form on Your Website" page does not say where submissions from an embedded form go. The closest statements are on the Lead Tracking page (filling out a Marketo form associates activity with a known lead) and the Forms API Reference (the form is loaded from Marketo servers). No Adobe sentence found stating that an embedded form creates or updates a person in the Marketo database in those words.

B1: No licensing statement found for embedding a Marketo form on a non-Marketo page beyond "You must have a Marketo account to use these capabilities." on the Marketo Developer Guide JavaScript API page (not included as a fact).

B4: helpx.adobe.com/legal/product-descriptions pages (aem-cloud-service.html and others) return 403 Access Denied from this environment, so no quote could be taken from the product descriptions. The word "add-on" for AEM Forms relative to AEM Sites was not found on Experience League; the pages say the solutions are "licensed individually" and that Forms use needs "a valid AEM Forms license".
cautions: The migration journey, Best Practices Analyzer, Cloud Acceleration Manager migration steps and Content Transfer Tool all assume the source is AEM (CTT: AEM 6.3 or higher, on-premise or AMS). If the bank is not on AEM, they do not apply. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/migration-journey/getting-started

Experience Modernization Agent limits: "The skills target Edge Delivery Services only."; AEM publish environments with HTL-based delivery and headless delivery are unsupported targets; sites behind a VPN or firewall are unsupported sources; third-party integrations, MarTech data layer, multisite inheritance (MSM) and custom functionality need manual effort; protected site authentication "is not intended for use with personally identifiable information (PII) or real end-user data" (relevant for a bank). Status on the page: "The self-service Experience Modernization Console is generally available." https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/ai-in-aem/agents/brand-experience/modernization/overview

AOE delivery is an optional Adobe engineer-led service, and its sources must be public static HTML: "Intranet sites, password-protected content, and VPN-only systems are not accessible." It may overlap with partner migration services. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/ai-in-aem/agents/brand-experience/modernization/aoe-delivery

AEM Importer: "Please note that only Chrome-based browsers are supported."; the JCR packages are binaryless (assets are imported separately with the AEM Import Helper); for 10k+ URLs Adobe says to contact the AEM team. https://www.aem.live/developer/importer

Core Components pages (Sites and Adaptive Forms) carry a tip: "You can continue using the methods described in this document for existing projects. However for new projects, Adobe recommends leveraging Edge Delivery Services." https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-core-components/using/introduction

Universal Editor: "the Universal Editor intends to eventually supersede the Page Editor"; its two primary supported setups are Edge Delivery Services (preferred) and headless implementations. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/implementing/developing/universal-editor/introduction

Marketo embedded forms: prefill does not work with the embed code; per a Marketo KB article, embedded forms do not load when JavaScript is disabled. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-cloud-kcs/kbarticles/ka-28517

AEM Forms to Marketo: only the People (Leads) database is supported, and custom objects only if associated with the Lead database. The videos on these pages apply to Core Components only. The pages use both "Submit to Marketo" and "Submit to Marketo Engage" for the action name. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/forms/integrate/set-submit-action/integrate-adaptive-form-with-market-engage/integrate-form-to-marketo-engage

For AEM Forms on Edge Delivery Services, the Marketo submit action is listed under AEM Publish Submission (form data goes to the AEM as a Cloud Service Publish instance), not the simple Forms Submission Service. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/edge-delivery/build-forms/configure-submission-action-for-eds-forms
The go-live checklist notes that WAF rules "require a separate license". https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-cloud-service/content/onboarding/journey/go-live-checklist
Dates: page dates are the "Last update" shown on each page when fetched on Nov 10 2026; aem.live pages show no date.
